idiom_name: WeakMap/WeakSet typed through lib ES2015.Collection; WeakRef<T> and FinalizationRegistry through lib ES2021.WeakRef
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds types, not semantics. WeakMap<K extends object, V> arrives with lib ES2015.Collection, while WeakRef<T extends object> and FinalizationRegistry come with lib ES2021.WeakRef (or ES2021/ESNext), so the tsconfig lib option is the capability floor for the weak-reference realization: a project targeting ES2020 primitives can still use weak references by adding ES2021.WeakRef to lib. The typings make absence part of the interface (`deref(): T | undefined`, `get(k): V | undefined`), which is the typed form of obtain a strong reference before use and tolerate absence, and keying semantics remain the runtime's (object or non-registered-symbol keys, no enumerability).
pitfalls: The types describe a possibility, not a guarantee: deref(): T | undefined and get(): V | undefined must be narrowed at every use, and no type can make the engine collect on schedule.

Declaring WeakRef without adding ES2021.WeakRef (or ES2021/ESNext) to lib fails to compile, and a mis-set target does not change the runtime - the typed floor and the runtime floor are configured separately.
WeakMap typing accepts any object key, including one you keep alive for the whole program: the type system cannot stop you from being the strong owner yourself.
Type-only abstractions over weak edges (a branded WeakRef<T> alias, an interface with a deref method) add no safety over the built-in types and hide that the operation may fail.

variants.name: WeakRef<T> + FinalizationRegistry cache (lib ES2021.WeakRef)
variants.idiom_name: Map<K, WeakRef<V>> swept by a FinalizationRegistry, typed through lib ES2021.WeakRef
variants.implementation_notes: For value-keyed caches the typed realization is a strong Map of WeakRef<V> entries: the type parameter is bounded to objects, deref() returns V | undefined, and the FinalizationRegistry callback receives the held key and must re-check the entry before deleting it. The lib entry ES2021.WeakRef is required for the declarations, and the tsconfig target must actually emit code for a runtime that has them - TypeScript never polyfills: an ES2021 lib on an ES5 target compiles but ships calls the old runtime cannot make.
pitfalls: lib only supplies declarations: compiling ES2021 typings for an older runtime ships code that throws at run time - the target/runtime must provide WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry.
The registry callback is not synchronous and may never run, so the Map can retain stale WeakRef entries; pair it with a size bound or a periodic sweep.
deref() is a snapshot for the current job, and a live entry re-inserted under the same key must not be deleted by a late callback - always re-check before deleting.
